Subject (in full) Riverside Power Station gives notice of decision to delay the
collection of loans made to employees.

Made by D. S. I. Cash Forwarded by

Sir,

The following is the text of a notice in English and Chinese which
was posted by the management of the Shanghai Power Company at the
Riverside Station at 5 p.m. February 1, 1934.

Notice to Employees

"Some of the employees of the company have directly appealed to
the company for temporary assistance at this time.
As the company at all times wishes to be fair to its employees
and realizes that during the winter and at new year time expenses
are high, the company has decided to delay collecting the loans
made to employees until July 1934. Employees leaving the company's
service before July 1934 will repay their loan from any money which
may be due them when leaving.
Employees should understand that the company is doing this to
help them at this time and is not cancelling the loans made to
employees."

Copy for A.C. Special Branch forwarded.

D. S. I.

the wages two months after date. The
mediators will be responsible that the
labourers will receive one month's pay

3. Chinese members of the Council will
negotiate over the conditions when the
labourers resumed work.

4. The mediators will be responsible that
all those who were dismissed will receive
their retirement gratuity and back pay.

5. Those who resume work need not be worried
even they had nothing to do, they will

work

Made by and Forwarded by Det. Insp. A. Telfer.

Sir,
The situation among the employees of the various departments
at the Shanghai Power Company Depot, Nos. 30/1 Fearon Road up to
9.30 a.m. on November 2nd., 1933 is as follows:-

| | Regular employees (Chinese) Total | No. reported for duty on the morning of November 2nd. 1933 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Operating Division | 411 | 96 (1 less) |
| Transport Section | 153 | 76 (6 temporary employees) |
| Meter Department | 107 | 31 (13 less) |
| Stores | 29 | 13 (2 temporary employees) |
| Consumers Office | 129 | 3 |
| | 829 | 219 |

Out of the 59 regular Chinese employees who reported for duty
on October 31st., 1933, 14 of them did not appear at their various
positions on November 2nd., 1933. The reason for the latter number
of employees not coming into work is owing to the intimidation by
the representatives from the Strike Union, who apparently have been
going to their homes, but where such cases are brought to light
Police protection is given.

At 6 p.m. on November 1st., 1933 a notice in English and
Chinese which reads as follows:-

"Beginning Friday November 3rd. the Shanghai Power Company.
will commence the employment of men to permanently fill vacancies.
Employees who were forced to strike through intimidation will
be given preference to such employment"

were posted at the entrances of the following places around the
Depot:-

Main Entrance Fearon Road
Meter Department Fearon Road near Yuhang Road
Consumers Workshop Yuhang Road

Sir,

The situation of the employees at the Shanghai Power Company
Depot, Nos. 30/1 Jesson Road up to 9.30 a.m. on November 1st., 1933
is as follows:-

regular employees No. reported for duty on the

Out of the 59 regular Chinese employees (referred to in my
report dated October 31st., 1933) who returned to their various
positions on October 31st., 1933 only 2 did not report for duty on
November 1st., 1933. It appears those regular employees who have
returned to their jobs within the past two days, some of their
families have been intimidated by Strike Union representatives to
the effect that if they did not keep their husbands from going to
their work they would be kidnapped with their children and also the
furniture in their homes taken to an unknown address. In such
cases coming to light the Special Branch, Headquarters, are being
informed by the Shanghai Power Company who in turn will instruct
the station concerned where the employee lives for necessary
protection to be provided. Ten (10) more regular workers reported
for duty at the "Meter Department" of above Depot after 9.30 p.m.
on October 31st., 1933, but on the morning of November 1st., 1933

Sir,

At 3 p.m. 18/10/33 representatives of the General Labour Union entertained at Dah Si Yang (大西陽) Restuarant, Foochow Road about 20 Press Representatives. Ts Yah Van (朱学範) presided and in a speech requested the Press to assist in the strike.

The meeting ended at 4 p.m..

At 10 a.m. 18/10/33, 5 members of the strike Committee namely Nyi Yung Foo (倪文富), Woo Yu Sung (胡友生), Tsang Lung Sung, and two others names unknown visited the homes of Yoong Tsoong Kyung (榮宗敬), Li Foh Sung (李福壽), and Woo Ta Ngoh (鄔志豪) and requested them to mediate in the strike. The last three named persons are reported to hold a large number of shares in the S.P.C..

At 3 p.m. 18/10/33 representatives of various labour unions held a meeting at the Ningpoo Fellow Countryman Association, Thibet Road. Zung Tsung Chue (鄭正秋) presided. The advisability of aiding the S.P.C. strikers was discussed and it was decided to assist.

Subject (in full) Shanghai Power Company Strike.

Made by and Forwarded by Detective Inspector A. Telfer

Sir,

The situation at the Shanghai Power Company Depot, Nos. 30/1,
Fearon Road remains the same as given in my report dated October
10th 1933, with the exception of the clerical staff, who were
warned on the evening of October 10th 1933 by letter from the
Strike Committee to attend a meeting at 8 a.m. on October 11th,
1933 at the West Gate, Chinese City. Eight (8) of the staff
reported at the Depot before 8 a.m. on latter date and left
orderly informing Mr. W. Hunter, Assistant Distribution Engineer,
that they must attend owing to the fact their homes are nearby
where the Committee headquarters are at West Gate, and were afraid
of the consequences if they did not make an appearence. The
remainder of the clerical staff, four (4) in number, are remain-
ing in as they feel they are quite safe because they live in the Inter-
national Settlement.

The Shanghai Power Company Staff Association, it was learned
from Mr. W. Hunter, intended to hold a meeting of loyal workers
at 5 p.m. on October 11th 1933 at the Head Offices, Nanking Road
to review the strike situation and, it appears the Strike Commit-
tee heard of this and being afraid they (the loyal workers) may
be influenced not to support the strikers, therefore, called on
the clerical staff to attend the aforementioned meeting at the
West Gate.

During my visit to the above Depot between 8 a.m. and 8.40
a.m. on October 11th, 1933 there was no sign of trouble makers
nearby. The usual precautions are being taken by the Police.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Alexander Telfer

After 8 a.m. on 4/1 /33 a meeting was held at the Labour Union's Office, Foh Yu Road, Nantao and 50 odd foremen representing the strikers were present and the meeting was presided by 杨文富 Yee Yung Foo.

The following four resolutions were adopted at the meeting:-
(1) Foremen of various departments are not to employ any new workmen to work at the Power Stations.
(2) Foremen of various departments should warn all the workmen not to go back to work at the Power Stations.
(3) The Labour Union be requested to render assistance.
(4) To distribute pamphlets bearing the reasons for the strike to strikers as well as the public.

After 10 a.m. the 50 odd representatives led by 朱培生 Tsu Po Sang and 包德福 Pao Teh Tsao (workmen of Shanghai Power Coy.), 朱文彩 Tsu Yoo Vai, 叶祥老 Yeh Hsiang Kao (members of the staff of the Labour Union) proceeded to the Local K.M.T. Headquarters where they were received by Mr. Tai Yu Heng, a member of the above organization who promised to submit their suggestions to the committee.

Two workmen of the Fearon Road Power Station went back to work to-day and were stopped by some other others of the Riverside Power Station who took them to the Labour Union Office and asked that they be punished for breach of faith, and the result is at present unknown.

Mr. Heald of the S.P.C. requested the Local K.M.T. H'qters to ask the Labour Union to give permission to let four workmen go back to work (2 on day duty and 2 on night duty) to handle repairing work in cases of emergency; and the request was complied with and the four workmen have started working.

Subject (in full) Situation at the Riverside Power Station.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Willgoss.

Sir:-

Between 9 a.m. and 8 p.m. 1/1 /33 about 300 odd workers
registered their presence at the lectric Trade Union's Office. No.
12 Zeu Ying Fong Alleyway off Tirn Doong Road, Chapei. About 2000
workers from the Riverside Power Station and Fearon Road Power
Station went to the above office to get instructions as what to do
to-morrow.

Among the 300 workers present at the above office, somebody
suggested to damage the sub-stations at various points tomorrow but
others suggested to see Mr. Jones first at 9 o'clock tomorrow. If
no satisfactory reply is obtained, the strikers will start to damage
the sub-stations. 30 odd foremen and operatives will carry on work
as usual at the Fearon Road Station, but the remainder i.e.
carpenters, black-smith, fitters, machincs. etc will not work tomorrow

6 foremen of the Riverside Power Station will go back to work
as usual and the remainder will not work, except operatives who
remain loyal.

Means will be used to get the wives or relatives of the oper-
atives to go to the Riverside and Fearon Road Power Stations and
attempt to pursuade the operatives to leave their Work.

If no satisfactory reply is obtained from the S.M.C. Secretary-
's Office, the strikers will proceed to the S.P.C. Town Office for
a definate answer to their demand. A demonstration will probably
be held with slogans and pamphlets.

It is learned that the Chairman of the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce and some of the executive committees of the Local K.M.T.
Headquarters are holding confidential discussions to negotiate with
the S.P.Co. management to relieve the present situation and obtain
an amicable settlement.

雇佣条件之一规定：“任何非因自身过错而被解雇，或因工作量不足而被解雇的工人，将根据规章获得奖金。”不良行为、懒惰等情况违反这些规章。

1933年9月26日，一名在该厂服务约12年的钳工薛阿宝（Sih Ah Pao），因无法对缺勤超过3天给出令人满意的理由而被解雇。同时，另外两名工人，即在发动机房工作的戴仁恒（Tai Jen Heng）和在3号锅炉房工作的殷炳根（Ying Ping Keng），也于1933年9月27日因懒惰被解雇。这三人向管理层交涉，要求根据他们的服务年限支付应得的遣散费（gratuity），但管理层依据规章予以拒绝。

由于这一拒绝，工人们（主要是木匠、钳工和铁匠）指派了3名代表前往南市当地国民党党部，讨论未支付遣散费一事并寻求援助。国民党党部委派了一名

Interruption of Work:-

URGENT NEWS.

Fellow Workers:-

The unreasonable dismissal of workmen and the
cancellation of payment of bonus have recently occurred at the
New Engine Room. 3 workmen have been dismissed by the Manage-
ment without the bonus. The interview with the Management by
representatives of all the workmen has failed to produce a
satisfactory result.

Now the New Engine Room has started the oppression
of workers and if the 2 power houses do the same, the 2000 workers
will lose all their privileges and there is possibility that all
the workers will be oppressed. We hope that all the workers
will struggle and cooperate to fight for a successful ending.

Propaganda Dept. 28/9/33.
Choped by Committee of the 'Calling
for Aid' Association, Water &
